notes: Trusted upstream sources (draft §23). This file answers three questions and nothing else:
which host may be contacted, what artifact a (capability, version) maps to, and where the
expected digest is published.
It deliberately does NOT contain digests. A digest written next to a download and never
checked against anything is decoration; the only acceptable source of an expected digest is
a published checksum file, and that is what `checksum` points at (draft §23.3-1).
`provenance` and `integrity` are separate on purpose (§4.4:368). v1 does no signature
verification: `signature` stays null, and a digest is never described as a signature.
Growth path: only hosts and capabilities that were actually verified end up here. An entry
that has never been resolved successfully must not be added 'for completeness'. Each entry's
notes carry its own verification status, and a test requires that statement to be present.
Draft §72 measured the `archive` capability against the real upstream and removed its entry.
The artifact template was right (`7z<version_nodots>-extra.7z` exists: 7z2603-extra.7z), but
the upstream publishes no checksum *file* on an allowed host: `checksums.txt` and five other
plausible names return 404 for every tag probed, and a release carries no .txt asset at all.
The per-asset digests appear only in the release page UI, which `single`/`sha256sums` cannot
fetch and parse. A digest source that does not exist is worse than no entry at all: `archive`
is now a capability without a source, so `source resolve` answers NOT_FOUND(1) — 'a capability
without a source is a reference-only capability, not an installable one' — instead of surfacing
an HTTP 404 as PROVENANCE_FAILED(7).
